title: Canonical evaluation duality and preservation of augmented derived completion
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ be a ringed site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the unbounded derived category $D(R)$, its K-flat symmetric derived tensor, and its closed derived internal Hom [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $M\in D(R)$, put $D=R\mathcal Hom_R(M,R)$ and let $e:D\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M\to R$ be evaluation. Suppose that for every $N\in D(R)$ the canonical transpose
$$u_N:N\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_R(M,N)$$
of contraction with $e$ is an isomorphism. Define $c:R\to M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D$ as the element corresponding to $1_M$ under the closed adjunction and $u_M$.

Then, with the canonical associators and unitors suppressed, the actual maps $e,c$ satisfy
$$(1_M\otimes e)(c\otimes1_M)=1_M,\qquad(e\otimes1_D)(1_D\otimes c)=1_D.$$
They induce both tensor adjunctions $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-\dashv D\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ and $D\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-\dashv M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$. In particular $T_M=M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ preserves all products that exist and every sequential homotopy-limit cone.

More generally let $(B_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a tower of commutative $R$-algebra sheaves with compatible unit maps $R\to B_n$. Define $C_B(N)=R\varprojlim_n(N\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_n)$, with canonical map $\eta_N:N\to C_B(N)$. Here sequential derived limits mean the Roos/Milnor homotopy limits, the fibre of $1-t:\prod_nN_n\to\prod_nN_n$, with $t$ induced by the tower transitions [lem-pc-homotopy-limit-map]. The associators and canonical product/limit comparisons give a natural isomorphism
$$T_MC_B(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B(T_MN)$$
whose composite with $T_M(\eta_N)$ equals $\eta_{T_MN}$. Thus $T_M$ preserves the objects for which $\eta_N$ is an isomorphism. This includes derived $\pi$-complete objects for $B_n=R/(\pi^n)$, and also the finite-coefficient reduction tower used for a pulled-back completed integral coefficient sheaf.

proof.text: Write $[M,N]=R\mathcal Hom_R(M,N)$. The evaluation-normalized closed adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction] identifies the transpose of $u_M c$ with $(1_M\otimes e)(c\otimes1_M)$. By the definition of $c$, $u_Mc$ is the transpose of $1_M$. Injectivity of this adjunction bijection gives the first triangle identity $f:=(1_M\otimes e)(c\otimes1_M)=1_M$. All tensors below are derived, and the fixed symmetric associators and unitors are suppressed.

proof.text:
Put $h=(e\otimes1_D)(1_D\otimes c)$. Functoriality of tensor gives
$$e(h\otimes1_M)=e(1_D\otimes1_M\otimes e)(1_D\otimes c\otimes1_M)=e(1_D\otimes f)=e.$$
For the middle equality, interchange the two evaluations $e$ on $D\otimes M\otimes D\otimes M$: applying either evaluation first and then the other is $e\otimes e$ followed by $R\otimes R\cong R$. Curry the displayed equality under [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction]. Since $D=[M,R]$ and $e$ is its actual evaluation, the transpose of $e(h\otimes1_M)$ is $h$, and the transpose of $e$ is $1_D$. Thus $h=1_D$, the second triangle identity. This checks the maps themselves without local equality detection or a choice of duality data.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dual-tensor-adjunctions] to the exact pairing $(M,D,e,c)$ just verified. It gives $T_D\dashv T_M$ and $U_M\dashv U_D$, where $T_A=A\otimes-$ and $U_A=-\otimes A$. Symmetry identifies $U_A$ with $T_A$, so the latter adjunction is $T_M\dashv T_D$. The former makes $T_M$ a right adjoint and therefore proves preservation of all existing products (with their indexing sets in the chosen universe).

proof.text: The native derived tensor already has its canonical shift comparison and the proved source-library instance DerivedCategory.isTriangulated_tensorLeft (WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Monoidal.Shift). Transport from the chosen closed structure using its monoidal equality. Since step 3 makes tensorLeft M a right adjoint, it preserves countable products. Apply lem-pc-homotopy-limit-map directly. No comparison with the separate KFlatFixedTensorTriangulated presentation is required. For completion, lem-pc-kflat-resolution is used through the proved K-flat localization of the native closed-adjunction module: its inclusion followed by Q is a localization and hence essentially surjective.

proof.text: Construct a RoosLimit from lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit by taking its stated distinguished derived-limit triangles as Milnor cones. For a strict augmented algebra tower, tensoring a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes is a quasi-isomorphism by the native invertible tensorators and naturality. Localize this strict tensor-tower functor to obtain an augmented completion Model. Descend its whole augmentation transformation through the fully faithful whiskering functor of that localization. For a K-flat representative A of M, apply lem-sfb-kflat-augmented-roos-comparison. Identify its derived tensor functor with tensorLeft (Q A) using the native tensorator and fully faithful whiskering by Q. Right-adjoint product preservation from step 3 makes the Roos comparison invertible.

proof.text: For a K-flat P, construct the strict tower isomorphism (A tensor P) tensor X_n ≅ A tensor (P tensor X_n) from the ordinary tensor associator. Its naturality checks every transition. The tensor unitor and associator equations identify the whole ordinary-limit lifts of the augmentations, not just projections of a derived limit. Convert ordinaryLimit to roosLimitFunctor by its canonical limit-cone isomorphism and transport the right-derived universal comparison accordingly. Combine the Model computation, the normalized Roos comparison, the inverse strict associator, the Model computation on A tensor P (which is K-flat by associativity and the two K-flat hypotheses), and the native tensorator. Their composite preserves the entire Model.unit by unit_computes and the Roos augmentation equation. Fully faithful whiskering through the K-flat localization descends this natural isomorphism and its unit equation to every derived object. Essential surjectivity of that localization supplies a representative of M; tensoring its isomorphism transports the conclusion from Q A to M.

proof.text: If $\eta_N$ is an isomorphism, so is $T_M(\eta_N)$ because functors preserve inverses; its composite with $\theta_N$ is therefore an isomorphism. By step 6 this composite is precisely $\eta_{T_MN}$. This proves preservation of the complete objects for every algebra tower in the statement, including $B_n=R/(\pi^n)$ and the finite-coefficient reduction tower of a pulled-back completed integral coefficient sheaf. No assertion of underived exact products, flat quotients, or regularity of $\pi$ was needed.
